preamble: Middle Chinese voiced velar [g] (the 群 initial) before [i, y] devoiced and palatalized to aspirated [tɕʰ]. In Mandarin this happens only in the level tone (oblique-tone words have unaspirated [tɕ]); in Gan (e.g. Nanchang), where the voiced obstruents became voiceless aspirated in every tone, oblique-tone words show [tɕʰ] as well.

examples.note: Gan aspirates the reflexes of voiced obstruents in all tones, so oblique-tone 舊 has [tɕʰ], unlike Mandarin jiù [tɕ].

period: Middle Chinese to modern varieties (c. 600 CE onward)
